summary: The menu a right-click opens on a thing — a row's actions, a file's. Shift+F10 and the Menu key open it from the keyboard, under the thing. A shortcut to actions that are also reachable some other way.
useWhen: a thing already has an actions menu or buttons, and people who work in the list all day want them under the pointer — table rows, files, cards
the product feels like a desktop tool, where right-click is expected on the objects in it

useInstead.when: the actions are reachable only through the context menu
useInstead.why: nothing on the page says a right-click does anything, touch screens have none, and on iOS a long press opens the browser's callout. A context menu must never be the only way in — give the thing a visible ⋯ MenuTrigger with the same items

useInstead.when: a text field or a link whose own browser menu people use — copy, open in new tab, spelling
useInstead.why: replacing the browser's menu there takes away actions people rely on

composition.note: `children` is the one element the menu is for; `menu` is a Menu, usually the same one the element's ⋯ MenuTrigger opens, built once and used twice.

children.note: it receives `onContextMenu` and `onKeyDown`, and keeps its own; it is not wrapped, so a `<tr>` stays a `<tr>`

requires: `aria-label` naming the menu for its thing — "Actions for Invoice reconciler" — since no button names it
every action also reachable without the context menu — a ⋯ MenuTrigger on the thing, or buttons
guarantees: a right-click opens the menu at the pointer, and prevents the browser's menu on the element only
Shift+F10 or the Menu key, with focus on the element or anything in it, opens it under the element at its start edge — never at a pointer that is not there
focus moves to the first item; Escape, an outside click or choosing an item closes it and returns focus to where it was
a second right-click on the element moves the open menu there, with the browser's menu still prevented; one elsewhere closes ours and leaves the browser's
the menu is a full Menu: ↓ ↑ move between items across sections, and typing jumps to one
on a scrolled page the menu opens at the pointer
`isDisabled` leaves the browser's own menu in place
notes: Shift+F10 is caught as a key because not every browser turns it into a contextmenu event; the Menu key arrives as a keyboard contextmenu and is anchored to the element
the element needs something focusable inside it — a link, a checkbox — for Shift+F10 to reach it from the keyboard

antiPatterns.dont: actions that exist only in the context menu
antiPatterns.do: the same Menu behind a visible ⋯ MenuTrigger, and ContextMenu as the shortcut
antiPatterns.why: a right-click is invisible and unavailable on touch; an action there alone is an action most people never find

antiPatterns.dont: a ContextMenu around the whole page or a large region
antiPatterns.do: one around each thing — each row, each file
antiPatterns.why: a menu for "the page" has no object; each item has to guess what it acts on, and the browser's useful menu is gone everywhere

antiPatterns.dont: a context menu with different items from the thing's ⋯ menu
antiPatterns.do: one Menu element passed to both
antiPatterns.why: two menus that disagree teach people that neither is complete
